blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a low-cost draft model to propose tokens that the full-size target model verifies in parallel.
Parallel and semi-autoregressive (semi-AR) drafters improve drafting efficiency by proposing an entire block in a single forward pass, but training them raises a new difficulty: the draft distribution for a given position depends on where the decoding round starts, and where rounds start depends on how many tokens earlier rounds accepted.
Existing training objectives typically rely on block-local surrogates that ignore this cross-round coupling, and therefore do not directly optimize the global decoding efficiency.
In this work, we develop a theoretical framework for training and evaluating these drafters by representing speculative decoding as a Markov reward process.
This formulation yields the Expected Decoding Rounds (EDR) objective, which weights local rejection costs by state occupancies and exactly equals the expected number of decoding rounds.
Unlike prior surrogate objectives, EDR introduces no auxiliary hyperparameters.
We then derive an exact temporal-difference gradient that supports unbiased stochastic optimization from target-model rollouts.
The same framework also yields an exact offline evaluator for round counts, enabling paired drafter comparisons on shared target rollouts without running speculative decoding.
Finetuning two state-of-the-art drafters, DSpark and DFly, with EDR consistently improves mean accepted length and outperforms existing training objectives across nine benchmarks spanning math reasoning, code generation, and chat.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Autoregressive (AR) generation is a central bottleneck in large language model (LLM) inference.
Since each token can be produced only after its preceding tokens are available, the number of function evaluations required to generate a text sequence grows linearly with its length.
blocks.zh:
自动回转(AR)生成是大语言模型(LLM)推论中的一个中心瓶颈.
由于每个令牌只能在获得之前的令牌后才能出出,生成文本序列所需的函数评价次数随其长度而呈线性增长.

blocks.en:
Speculative decoding ( Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) reduces this sequential cost by using a lightweight draft model to propose multiple candidate tokens, which the full-size target model verifies in parallel in a single forward pass.
With rejection-sampling verification, the generated sequence follows the target model’s distribution exactly.
Therefore, speculative decoding accelerates inference without sacrificing quality, and the goal is to reduce expensive target model verifications—equivalently, decoding rounds—while keeping drafting itself inexpensive.
blocks.zh:
分型解码(Leviathan等,2023;Chen等,2023)通过使用轻量级的草案模型来提出多个候选标志来降低这种相继成本,而全尺寸的目标模型在一次前行传中同时验证.
通过拒绝抽样验证,生成的序列完全遵循目标模型的分布.
因此,投机性解码在不牺牲质量的情况下加快推论,目标是减少昂贵的目标模式核查——相当于解码回合——同时保持起草本身的成本。

blocks.en:
Early work employed AR drafters ( Li et al., 2024b ) that predict draft tokens sequentially, so the latency contributed in the drafting phase grows linearly with the draft block size.
To reduce the sequential work of drafting, parallel drafters ( Cai et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2026a ) have emerged to propose multiple draft tokens in one forward pass, typically built on masked diffusion language models ( Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2024 ) .
Their semi-AR variants ( Cheng et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) add limited sequential dependence within each draft block to improve the draft quality.
Parallel drafting supports longer draft blocks and deeper drafter networks, with potential to significantly accelerate the inference of a large target model.
blocks.zh:
早期的工作雇用了AR起草者(Li等,2024b),他们依次预测出草稿的符号,因此在起草阶段的暂时性贡献随着草稿块大小的线性增长.
为了减少相继的起草工作,出现了平行的起草者(Cai等,2024;Chen等,2026a)在一出前传中提出多出代号草案,典型的是基于遮掩的传播语言模型(Sahoo等,2024;Shi等,2024.).
他们的半AR变体 (Cheng等, 2026;Liu等, 2026)在每个编组中增加有限的相继依赖,以提高编组的质量.
平行的起草支持较长的区块草稿和更深的起草者网络,有可能大大地加快大目标模型的推论.

blocks.en: For a fixed architecture, a drafter’s quality affects inference speed primarily through the number of decoding rounds, so the natural training objective is to minimize the expected number of rounds.
blocks.zh: 对于固定的建筑,起草者的质量主要通过解码弹的数量来影响推断速度,因此自然训练的目标是将预期的弹数降到最低.

blocks.en:
For an AR drafter, the proposal at position t t is conditioned on the full realized prefix x < t x_{<t} regardless of where the current round started, so its acceptance probability depends only on this prefix.
As a result, the standard local training objective for AR drafters—matching the target model’s next-token distribution at every prefix—is directly aligned with this goal ( Yin et al., 2024a ) .
In contrast, for a parallel or semi-AR drafter, the proposal can instead depend on an earlier prefix x ≤ n x_{\leq n} with n < t n<t (in a round starting at n n ), with access to only some or none of the intermediate tokens.
Consequently, the same output position can have different draft distributions depending on where the round starts.
blocks.zh:
对于一个AR起草者来说,t t t位置上的提议以完全实现的前缀 x < t x_{<t}为条件,而不论当前回合是从哪里开始的,因此其接受概率只取决于这个前缀.
因此,AR起草者的标准当地培训目标——与目标模型在每个前缀的下接接分布相匹配——与这一目标直接一致(Yin等人,2024a) 。 。 。 。
相形之下,对于一个平行或半AR的起草者,提案则可以依赖更早的前缀 x ≤ n x_{\leq n}与 n < t n < t (从 n 开始的一回合),只能访问部分或没有中间的符.
因此,同一产出位置可以根据回合开始地点的不同而有不同的草稿分配。

blocks.en:
This additional dependence breaks the direct link between local distribution matching and global decoding efficiency.
The draft for position t t from a round starting at n n matters only if the decoding trajectory first reaches a round starting at n n and then accepts all preceding draft tokens in that round up to position t − 1 t-1 .
Both events depend on earlier acceptance outcomes induced by the drafter itself.
Thus, changing the drafter affects both acceptance within a round and which draft distributions are encountered in subsequent rounds, making the training objective inherently coupled across rounds.
blocks.zh:
这种额外的依赖性打破了本地发行匹配与全球解码效率之间的直接联系.
只有在解码轨迹首先从n到n,然后在该回合中接受所有先前的代号草案,直至 t - 1 t - 1 时,从n 开始的一回合开始, t t 位置的草案才重要。
这两种情况都取决于起草者自己促成的早期接受结果。
因此,修改起草者既影响到一轮内接受,又影响到以后几轮中遇到哪些草案分发,使培训目标在本质上相互配合。

blocks.en:
However, existing objectives for parallel and semi-AR drafters do not account for these cross-round dependencies and instead rely on local surrogates.
Examples include the expected number of tokens accepted within a single round ( Li et al., 2026c ) and draft-target distributional discrepancies under hand-crafted weights ( Chen et al., 2026a ; Wu et al., 2026 ) .
This motivates the central question: Can we train parallel and semi-AR drafters by directly minimizing the expected number of decoding rounds?
blocks.zh:
然而,平行和半AR起草者的现有目标并没有考虑到这些交叉回合的依赖性,而是依赖于当地代词.
例如,在一回合内(Li等,2026c)接受的预期令牌数量和手动权重下的草稿-目标分配差异(Chen等,2026a; 吴等,2026).
这引发了核心问题: 我们能否通过直接将预期的解码弹数减少到最低程度来训练平行和半AR起草器?

blocks.en:
We answer this question affirmatively.
Our approach relies on two key observations. First, conditioned on the output sequence, speculative decoding with a parallel or semi-AR drafter can be formulated as a Markov reward process (MRP) ( Howard, 1971 ) : each state records where the current round started and which position is being verified, and each rejection costs one round. Second, since rejection-sampling verification ensures that the output follows the same target distribution for every drafter, averaging over target rollouts recovers the expected number of rounds of actual decoding.
Together, these insights allow us to capture the dependencies across decoding rounds explicitly and characterize the expected number of decoding rounds exactly, yielding a unified framework for training and evaluating drafters.
blocks.zh:
我们肯定地回答这个问题。
我们的方法依靠两个关键的意见。 首先,以输出序列为条件,与平行或半AR起草器的投机解码可以被制定为马可夫奖励过程(MRP,1971年). :每个州记录本轮开始和正在核实哪个位置,每个拒绝都花费一回合. 第二,由于拒绝抽样核查确保每个起草者的产出都遵循相同的目标分布,因此平均比目标推出回收实际解码的预期数。
这些洞察力使我们能清楚地了解各轮解码工作的依赖性,并准确地描述预期的解码工作次数,从而形成一个统一的培训和评价起草者的框架。

blocks.en:
Building on this framework, we introduce the Expected Decoding Rounds (EDR) objective, whose minimization is equivalent to minimizing the expected number of decoding rounds.
We then derive a temporal-difference gradient estimator, enabling drafter training from target-model rollouts.
EDR applies across drafter architectures and introduces no hyperparameters.
We further prove that drafters maximizing the expected accepted length for each round can be strictly suboptimal for EDR, theoretically justifying the advantages of our global objective.
The framework also yields an exact offline evaluator of expected round counts, enabling comparisons of drafters on the same target-model rollouts without running online speculative decoding.
blocks.zh:
在这个框架的基础上,我们引入了"预期解码回合"(EDR)目标,其最小化相当于将预期的解码回合数降到最低.
然后,我们从目标模式的推出中得出一个时间差梯度估计值,使起草者能够接受培训。
EDR适用于起草器架构,没有引入超参数.
我们进一步证明,为每一回合尽量扩大预期接受的长度的起草者,对东德来说,在理论上可以证明我们全球目标的好处。
该框架还产生一个准确的离线评价员,对预期的圆计数进行线下评价,从而能够在不进行在线投机解码的情况下,在同一目标模式推出时对起草者进行比较。

blocks.en:
Empirically, we finetune two state-of-the-art (SOTA) drafters, DSpark ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) and DFly ( Liu et al., 2026 ) , with EDR
while keeping their architectures and inference procedures unchanged. Across nine benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, code generation, and chat, a single epoch of EDR finetuning consistently improves mean accepted length over the original drafters and existing training objectives.
blocks.zh:
以经验论,我们微调了两个最先进的(SOTA)起草者,DSpark(成等,2026年)和DFly(刘等,2026年),EDR.
同时保持它们的架构和推论程序不变. 在涉及数学推理、代码生成和聊天的9个基准中,一个单一的EDR微调时代不断改善,意味着接受的长度超过了最初的起草者和现有的培训目标。

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • A Markov reward process formulation. We provide a theoretical framework that exactly characterizes expected speculative decoding rounds for parallel and semi-AR drafters. • An exact and trainable global objective. We introduce EDR, establish its equivalence to minimizing the expected number of decoding rounds, derive a tractable gradient for drafter training, and prove its advantage over local surrogates. • An exact offline evaluator. We provide an offline evaluator of the expected number of decoding rounds, enabling paired evaluation of drafters on the same target-model rollouts. • Consistent empirical gains. EDR finetuning improves two SOTA drafters across nine benchmarks, outperforming existing training objectives.

blocks.en:
The latency per generated token depends on the accepted length per
round as well as the costs of drafting and verification.
Architectural work therefore seeks to increase accepted length while
keeping drafting inexpensive.
Medusa ( Cai et al., 2024 ) attaches multiple prediction heads to
target-model features, while Hydra ( Ankner et al., 2024 ) introduces
sequential dependencies between these heads to improve draft accuracy.
EAGLE-3 ( Li et al., 2026d ) combines features from multiple target layers.
To reduce sequential drafting overhead, parallel and diffusion-based
drafters generate multiple proposals in a single forward pass.
DFlash ( Chen et al., 2026a ) uses a lightweight block-diffusion drafter
conditioned on target-model context features.
DiffuSpec ( Li et al., 2026a ) repurposes a pretrained diffusion language model as
a parallel drafter and uses causal-consistency path search to
construct proposals for autoregressive verification.
To improve within-block consistency without returning to fully
autoregressive drafting, DSpark ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) and
DFly ( Liu et al., 2026 ) combine parallel backbones with lightweight
sequential heads that condition on preceding draft tokens.

blocks.en:
Drafter training commonly uses cross-entropy or KL-divergence
objectives to align draft predictions with the target distribution ( Li et al., 2026d ; Chen et al., 2026a ) .
However, distributional matching under these losses does not
necessarily maximize token acceptance when drafter capacity is limited.
LK losses ( Samarin et al., 2026 ) address this distinction through
acceptance-oriented objectives.
For multi-token drafting, the first rejection invalidates all
subsequent proposals in the block, making the contributions of
different positions unequal.
DFlash ( Chen et al., 2026a ) accounts for this asymmetry using fixed
exponentially decaying position weights.
D-PACE ( Wu et al., 2026 ) replaces this fixed schedule with adaptive weights
derived from a differentiable accepted-length surrogate based on
draft confidences.
The end-to-end (E2E) multi-step TV loss ( Li et al., 2026c ) moves beyond
independent token-level matching by incorporating the multiplicative
structure of acceptance across positions within a block.
Recent work addresses the mismatch between drafter training and
inference by incorporating verification feedback.
Draft-OPD ( Lei et al., 2026 ) replays draft proposals from

blocks.en:
Diffusion language models (DLMs) ( Nie et al., 2025 ; Inception Labs et al., 2025 ; Ye et al., 2025 ) offer an alternative to AR generation by iteratively refining sequences with bidirectional context, enabling parallel token generation.
Continuous DLMs ( Li et al., 2022 ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Li et al., 2026b ) extend continuous diffusion models ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Song et al., 2020b ; Song et al., 2020a ) and flow matching ( Lipman et al., 2022 ) to token embedding spaces. Starting from Gaussian noise, they generate continuous token representations through learned denoising or flow dynamics, then map these representations to discrete tokens. This framework facilitates adapting established techniques for controlling and accelerating diffusion sampling, including classifier-free guidance ( Ho and Salimans, 2022 ) , self-conditioning ( Chen et al., 2022 ) , few-step solvers ( Lu et al., 2022 ; Li and Cai, 2024 ; Jiao et al., 2026 ) , and distillation ( Song and Dhariwal, 2024 ; Yin et al., 2024b ) .
Discrete DLMs ( Lou et al., 2023 ; Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2024 ) operate directly in token space using categorical corruption.
Masked DLMs belong to this category and corrupt sequences by replacing tokens with a special mask token. Then it generate text by progressively unmasking multiple positions in parallel. This formulation underlies many parallel and semi-AR drafters.
However, conditionally independent sampling within an update can overlook dependencies among simultaneously generated tokens, creating a trade-off between generation quality and sampling efficiency ( Li and Cai, 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Dmitriev et al., 2026 ; Zhao and Cai, 2026 ; Cai and Li, 2026 ) .

连续DLMs(Li等,2022;Chen等,2026b;Li等,2026b) 将连续扩散模型(Ho等,2020;Song等,2020b;Song等,2020a)和流量相配(Lipman等,2022年)扩展为象征嵌入空间. 从高斯噪声开始,它们通过所学的去诺或流动来产生连续的符号表示,再将这些表示物映射到离散的符号上. 这一框架有助于调整控制并加速扩散取样的既定技术,包括无分级指导(Ho and Salimans, 2022年),自理(Chen等人, 2022年),几步解析器 (Lu等,2022;Li和Cai等,2024;Jiao等,2026),并分馏(宋和达里瓦尔等,2024;殷等等,2024b.

Table 2 shows that EDR consistently improves speculative decoding across both DSpark and DFly without modifying the drafter architecture.
Compared with E2E finetuning, EDR achieves higher or equal MAL across all benchmarks, with larger gains on AIME25, LiveCodeBench, and the chat benchmarks.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced Expected Decoding Rounds (EDR), an exact global training objective for parallel and semi-AR speculative drafters.
By formulating speculative decoding as a Markov reward process conditioned on target-model outputs, we derived a tractable gradient for directly minimizing the expected number of verification rounds, together with an exact offline evaluator for paired draft-model comparison.
Empirically, EDR consistently improves two strong drafters, DSpark and DFly, across nine benchmarks without modifying their architectures or inference procedures, and outperforms the E2E training objective in overall mean accepted length.
These results suggest that explicitly accounting for cross-round dependencies provides a principled and practical direction for training more efficient parallel speculative draft models.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了 " 预期解码回合 " (EDR),这是对平行和半AR投机性起草者的精确全球培训目标。
通过制定以目标模型产出为条件的推测性解码为马尔可夫奖励过程,我们得出了可拉动的梯度,可以直接将预期的核查回合数降到最低,同时对成对的模型草案进行比较的精确离线评价。
从经验上讲,EDR不断改进两个强大的起草者,DSpark和DF,跨越了9个基准,没有修改其结构或推论程序,在总体平均接受长度上超过了E2E培训目标.
这些结果表明,明确考虑跨回合的依赖性,为培训更有效的平行投机性模型草案提供了原则性的实际方向。

blocks.en:
We conclude with several directions for future work.
First, our current framework focuses on a fixed draft block size.
However, under high-concurrency serving, verifying long draft blocks can become inefficient, especially when many later proposals are likely to be rejected.
Adaptive block sizing can reduce unnecessary verification by shortening the draft block when confidence is low, thereby further reducing inference latency ( Hu et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2024 ) .
An important direction is to extend our framework to adaptive block sizes and to study whether the optimal block size can be selected dynamically for each decoding round.
Second, EDR requires computing occupancy weights ω \omega and value functions V V for multiple anchor positions.
This is more computationally expensive than block-local objectives.
It would be interesting to explore more efficient ways to utilize the occupancy and value computations.
Finally, as shown in Table 2 , MAL varies substantially across datasets, suggesting that some target distributions are intrinsically more difficult to draft than others.
Our current work focuses on optimizing the drafter given a target distribution, but does not provide a complete theoretical characterization of this difficulty.
A promising direction is to identify properties of the target distribution that determine the best achievable speculative decoding efficiency.
blocks.zh:
最后,我们提出今后工作的几个方向。
第一,我们目前的框架侧重于固定的块大小草案。
然而,在高通货性服务下,核查长长的区块可能会变得效率低下,特别是在许多后来的提案可能会被否决的情况下.
适应性块大小化可以在信任度低时缩短块草稿,从而可减少不必要的核查,从而进一步减少推断延迟(Hu等,2026;Huang等,2024)。
一个重要的方向是把我们的框架扩大到适应性的块大小,并研究是否能够为每轮解码工作动态地选择最佳块大小.
第二,EDR要求计算多个锚地位置的入座权重 QQ\ omega和值函数 V V.
这比块-局部目标更昂贵。
探索更有效地利用占用和价值计算的方法将很有意义。
最后,如表2所显示的,《仲裁示范法》各数据集差异很大,表明有些目标分布在本质上比其他分布更为困难。
我们目前的工作重点是优化给定目标分布的起草器,但并没有为这一困难提供完整的理论特征。
一个有希望的方向是确定目标分布的属性,以确定最佳可实现的投机解码效率。

blocks.en: C.1 Draft EOS Probability Does Not Reduce EDR

blocks.en:
For the EDR objective, a correctly drafted terminal <EOS> does not save a
target-model verification round. Conditional on reaching the terminal
position, accepting a drafted <EOS> terminates in the current verification
pass. If the draft instead misses <EOS> , the correction branch can generate <EOS> in that same pass and terminates before another round starts. The same
holds when the terminal token is produced as the target bonus token after
block exhaustion. Accordingly, the EDR sum runs only over ordinary-token
positions t ≤ L t\leq L .
